name: Florida
$scopeNote: Florida has NO state individual wage income tax -- a constitutional prohibition (Fla. Const. Art. VII, sec. 5), not a mere policy choice. Never has had one.

sources.title: Florida Department of Revenue -- Reemployment Tax Rate Information
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Quoted verbatim: taxable wage base 'up to $7,000 per employee', new employer rate 'the initial tax rate is 0.0270 (2.7%). This rate remains in place until the employer has reported for 10 quarters', minimum rate '0.0010 (0.1%) or $7 per employee', maximum rate '0.0540 (5.4%) or $378 per employee'. Florida calls this 'Reemployment Tax' (renamed from Unemployment Compensation tax in 2012) and, unusually among the states in this project, it is administered by the Department of REVENUE, not a labor/workforce agency.

sources.title: Florida Paid Family Leave Insurance Act -- cross-source
sources.verifiedBy: Cross-source confirmed only, not independently fetched from a Florida statute this pass. Authorizes VOLUNTARY private paid-family-leave insurance products -- no state fund, no mandatory payroll deduction. Real structural finding beyond the usual 'no mandatory program': Florida law affirmatively PREEMPTS local governments from creating their OWN paid-leave mandates too (a state law barring cities/counties from filling the gap), a stronger preemption than most 'no local program' states in this project, which are simply silent on local authority rather than actively barring it.

exemptPretaxComment: Not applicable -- no income tax exists for any pretax category to reduce the base of.

reciprocity.note: Not applicable -- Florida has no income tax to be reciprocal about, same convention as this project's other no-income-tax states (SD, TN).

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE, and constitutionally barred. No Florida city or county levies, or may levy, a tax on wages or earned income.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE mandatory, and none permitted locally either. The Florida Paid Family Leave Insurance Act authorizes licensed insurers to OFFER voluntary paid-leave policies -- no state fund, no mandatory deduction (same voluntary-insurance-only shape as South Carolina's Act 206 and Tennessee's 2023 Act). Florida additionally preempts local governments from creating their own paid-leave mandates, a real structural fact beyond the bare absence of a state program -- not independently verified against the actual preemption statute this pass.

unemploymentInsurance.$comment: Florida calls this Reemployment Tax, not UI/SUTA -- administered by the Department of Revenue (unusual; every other state in this project uses a labor/workforce/employment-security agency). Employer-only, confirmed directly.
unemploymentInsurance.newEmployerRateNote: Applies until the employer has reported for 10 full quarters (2.5 years), per FL DOR's own page.
unemploymentInsurance.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- floridarevenue.com's own Reemployment Tax Rate Information page, fetched directly.
unemploymentInsurance.knownGap: Not modelled in the engine -- same structural note as every other state's employer SUTA in this project: experience-rated, an individual employer's actual rate depends on employer-specific history a static jurisdiction file can't hold.

knownGaps: The local-government paid-leave preemption is cross-source only, not independently verified against the actual Florida statute text this pass.
Given no income tax exists, this file is intentionally lighter-weight than income-tax states in this project -- consistent with the South Dakota/Tennessee precedent.
